Topic: Fourier Transform: The Mathematical Prism

Target audience: Undergraduate STEM students

Section: section_1 — The Intuitive Hook: The Smoothie Analogy (0:00-0:45)

Lecture lines:
A smoothie is just combined ingredients.
Signals are just combined sine waves.
Decompose them to find the ingredients.

Planned animations:
Fade in a blender icon #FFFFFF at center.
Display ingredients (vector arrows) in #FF5733 #33FF57 #3357FF around the blender.
Animate ingredients merging into the blender center.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Recap: Rotating Vectors (0:45-1:30)

Lecture lines:
Euler's formula connects circles and sine.
A vector rotating creates a wave.
Speed determines the frequency observed.

Planned animations:
Display two basis vectors i-hat #FFFF00 and j-hat #00FFFF.
Rotate i-hat and j-hat by 90 degrees counter-clockwise.
Highlight the path traced by the rotation using light gray #AAAAAA arcs.

Section: section_3 — The Mechanism: The Center of Mass (1:30-3:00)

Lecture lines:
Wrap a signal around a circle.
Adjust frequency to match the signal.
Center of mass shifts away.
This spike reveals the frequency.
The Fourier transform acts as prism.

Planned animations:
Place a set of points (masses) #FFFFFF in a 2D plane.
Calculate and draw the centroid (center of mass) in #FF00FF.
Move the points and show the centroid reacting in real-time.

Section: section_4 — Key Concept: Time Domain vs. Frequency Domain (3:00-4:00)

Lecture lines:
Time domain shows how things happen.
Frequency domain shows what things are.
Fourier transform bridges these two views.

Planned animations:
Display a time-domain wave signal #00FF00.
Transform signal into frequency components (bars) #FF00FF.
Display time-domain and frequency-domain plots side-by-side.

Section: section_5 — Application: Real-World Filtering (4:00-5:00)

Lecture lines:
Frequencies identify specific sound types.
Unwanted noise has unique high frequencies.
Remove these to clear your audio.

Planned animations:
Render a noisy signal #FF0000 on a graph.
Apply a low-pass filter (represented by a shaded block) #FFFFFF.
Display the cleaned signal #00FF00 output.

        self.place_at_grid(i_hat, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(j_hat, 'C2')
        
        # Group them for rotation
        vectors = VGroup(i_hat, j_hat)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Path
        arc = Arc(radius=1.0, start_angle=0, angle=PI/2, color="#AAAAAA")
        arc.move_to(self.grid['C2'])
        self.play(Create(arc))
        
        # Rotate
        self.play(Rotate(vectors, angle=PI/2, about_point=self.grid['C2']))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#AAAAAA"))
        self.wait(2)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: Real-World Filtering", ["Frequencies identify specific sound types.", "Unwanted noise has unique high frequencies.", "Remove these to clear your audio."])
        
        # Create graphs
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 10, 1], y_range=[-2, 2, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, 'C2')
        
        # Signal function (noisy)
        noisy_signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x) + 0.5 * np.sin(10 * x), color='#FF0000')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color('#FF0000')
        self.add(axes, noisy_signal)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color('#FFFFFF')
        # Represent low-pass filter (shaded box)
        filter_box = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color='#FFFFFF', fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(filter_box, 'C5')
        self.play(FadeIn(filter_box))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color('#00FF00')
        cleaned_signal = axes.plot(lambda x: np.sin(2 * x), color='#00FF00')
        self.play(Transform(noisy_signal, cleaned_signal), FadeOut(filter_box))
        self.wait(2)
